title: Coordinate With Maximum Network Quality
summary: Given an array of network towers with coordinates and quality factors, and a radius, find the coordinate with the maximum network quality.
statement: Given an array of network towers with coordinates and quality factors, and a radius, find the coordinate with the maximum network quality. The quality at a point is the sum of the signal qualities from all reachable towers, where a tower is reachable if the distance is within the radius. The signal quality is calculated as the floor of the tower's quality divided by one plus the distance. If multiple coordinates have the same quality, return the lexicographically smallest one. Lexicographical order first compares x-coordinates, then y-coordinates.
constraints: 1–50 towers at integer coordinates 0–50 with positive quality; radius is 1–50.
Sum floor(q/(1+distance)) from reachable towers. Return the lexicographically smallest coordinate with maximum quality.
hints: The bounded coordinate domain permits direct evaluation of every candidate point.
For each integer point 0..50 in lexicographic order, sum contributions from towers within the squared radius.
Update only for a strict quality improvement so the first tied coordinate remains.
Every eligible coordinate is visited and the signal formula is evaluated exactly; scan order proves the tie rule.
